correct_completion: she sent it to her manager.
full_sentence: Having finished her report, she sent it to her manager.
acceptable_variants: she then emailed it to her manager.
she handed it in to her manager.

options.text: she sends it to her manager.
options.why_wrong: 'Having finished' describes an action completed before the main action, so the main clause needs a past form, not a present one.

options.text: she sent it to her manager.
to send it to her manager.
options.why_wrong: The main clause needs a finite verb. An infinitive cannot complete the sentence after the participle clause.

options.text: the report was sent to her manager.
options.why_wrong: The subject of the main clause must be the person who finished the report. Here 'the report' creates a dangling participle.

explanation: A perfect participle clause shows that one action was completed before another action in the main clause. The subject of the participle clause must be the same as the subject of the main clause. Speakers who share a language with a different tense system may choose a present tense in the main clause by habit, so students should check the sequence of actions.
translation: Depois de terminar o relatório, ela o enviou à sua gerente.
